paras: For ordinary learning, start small—do shorter practices, make them warm, choose a small and tractable subject to work with, make sure you’re coming all the way back out of hypnosis, and track the effect on one target area (anxiety, chronic daydreaming, repairing a relationship, getting something done, sleep, emotional regulation, intuitive accuracy, etc.) for a week or two. If you find that your functioning worsens or you’re gaining certainty about memories that can’t be verified, then it’s time to reassess, not to push harder.

paras: Get some other appropriate help if you’re dealing with recurring panic attacks, compulsive behaviors, substance-related destabilization, or major relationship instability.
Methods to explore with a trained person present

If you want to deliberately use regression to explore the origins of a traumatic experience that you don’t know, to follow an affect or somatic bridge to unknown traumatic origins, or if you expect substantial flashback or dissociative reactions, work with a trauma-informed trained clinician who is trained in the method you’re using and who is present while you do it. (Affect and somatic bridges mean following associations from an emotional or bodily feeling; regression means remembering or imagining what it would have been like when you were younger. Both can also be used for more stable purposes, like finding resources.) Ask what they intend to do and how they’ll handle uncertainty and unexpected reactions. Even if you work with a clinician, please note that hypnosis can’t prove what did or didn’t happen in your life.

paras: Having a history of trauma, crying when you access inner children, or even wanting to feel difficult feelings, doesn’t necessarily mean you need more support than working on your own. paras: Most guidelines for treating major trauma emphasize treatments like trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy variants, cognitive processing therapy, prolonged exposure, or eye movement desensitization and reprocessing, depending on the person and the guideline. paras: The ultimate feedback on whether your process is working well is how you’re functioning in ordinary life. If you’re being more loving, honest, functional, relational, grounded, and precise than you were before you started, then keep going, gently. If you’re functioning less well than before, then stop trying to go deeper and focus instead on getting enough sleep, eating, grounding yourself, maintaining healthy boundaries with others, and getting support from others.
